publications.title: ESMA finalises the review of guidelines on the delay in disclosure of inside information
publications.summary: ESMA finalises the review of guidelines on the delay in disclosure of inside information 16 October 2026 Guidelines and Technical standards Market Abuse Market Integrity Simplification and Burden Reduction The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, has updated and streamlined its Market Abuse Regulation (MAR) guidelines on the delay in the disclosure of inside information , completing the revised regulatory framework. Under MAR, issuers are required to disclose as soon as possible the inside information concerning them, to ensure that investors are informed and to prevent insider dealing. In specific circumstances, issuers may delay public disclosure to avoid prejudicing their legitimate interests. publications.title: One year to go for T+1 settlement: the regulatory framework is complete, now let’s make it happen
publications.summary: One year to go for T+1 settlement: the regulatory framework is complete, now let’s make it happen 16 October 2026 Guidelines and Technical standards Post Trading Press Releases The European Union (EU) will switch to T+1 settlement on 11 October 2027. Ahead of the transition, the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, calls on market participants to finalise technical preparations, assess readiness across their entire ecosystems and begin testing as soon as possible throughout the trading and settlement chain. With the publication of the RTS and ESMA Guidelines on standardised procedures and messaging protocols , the regulatory framework is now ready. The first deadline is for investment firms and their clients to comply with the new requirements on allocations and confirmations from 7 December 2026. Verena Ross, ESMA’s chair

publications.title: RBI approves amalgamation of Indian branches of Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C. with RBL Bank Limited
publications.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has sanctioned the Scheme of Amalgamation of Indian branches of Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C. (Transferor Bank) with RBL Bank Limited (Transferee Bank). The Scheme has been sanctioned in exercise of the powers contained in sub-section (4) of Section 44A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. The effective date of the amalgamation shall be December 01, 2026. All the Indian branches of Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C. will function as branches of RBL Bank Limited with effect from December 01, 2026. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1342

publications.title: Offshore forwards and exchange rate transmission in emerging markets
publications.summary: We study how offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) markets transmit exchange-rate pressures to domestic currency markets. Using unique transaction-level data on the universe of centrally cleared NDFs for ten emerging-market currencies over 2013–2025, we show that offshore NDF order flow moves both offshore forward and domestic spot exchange rates and widens the offshore–onshore forward spread.

publications.summary: ESMA updates its manual on transparency with new guidance for OTC derivatives and tick-size regime 15 October 2026 Trading The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU regulator and supervisor, has updated its manual on transparency to provide further guidance on the identification of over-the-counter (OTC) derivatives subject to transparency requirements and to enhance supervisory convergence on the application of the tick-size regime. publications.title: ESMA's third Sanctions Report highlights the need for greater convergence in enforcement
publications.summary: ESMA's third Sanctions Report highlights the need for greater convergence in enforcement 15 October 2026 Market Abuse Supervisory convergence Transparency The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU's financial markets regulator and supervisor, published today its consolidated report on sanctions and measures imposed across the European Economic Area (EEA) in 2025, enhancing the transparency of sanctions data reported under EU financial acts within its remit. In 2025, national authorities across the EEA imposed more than 950 administrative sanctions and measures, a stable number compared with the past two years. The aggregated value of administrative fines amounted to almost €82 million. The report also highlights an increased use of settlements.
